title: qa.config.yaml
description: The one project-specific file this kit reads. Deliberately FLAT dotted keys (`a.b.c: value`), one per line, no nesting — the same no-third-party-dependency rule the harness holds itself to: a real YAML library is not required to parse it, so tools/run-qa-workflow.sh can read it with grep/cut alone and never fails because a dependency was not installed. Adding a field is tailoring; giving a value nested structure is not — flatten it to a dotted key instead.

project.name.description: Human-readable project name. Never used to branch logic — for display in reports only.

project.techStack.description: Free text, e.g. 'node-vue', 'flutter', 'node-graphql'. Also for display only; this kit never special-cases a stack.

harness.runCommand.description: Repo-relative command that runs the Agent Development Harness's gate floor and exits per its four-code contract, e.g. 'tools/qa/run-qa.sh'.

e2e.path.description: Repo-relative directory the E2E project lives in. Commands below run with this as their working directory.

e2e.regressionCommand.description: Command that runs the full/tagged regression suite, e.g. 'npm run test:regression'.

e2e.ticketCommand.description: Command template that runs cases scoped to one ticket ID; '{ticketId}' is substituted, e.g. 'npm test -- --grep {ticketId}'.

e2e.engines.description: Optional. Comma-separated list of browser/UI engines contributing to the E2E stage, e.g. 'playwright' or 'playwright,claude-in-chrome'. Defaults to 'playwright' alone when omitted — existing single-engine projects need no change. 'playwright' is scripted (driven by e2e.ticketCommand/e2e.regressionCommand, unchanged). 'claude-in-chrome' is agent-driven: it has no command; see e2e-engine-contract.md §8 and case-result.schema.json.

e2e.claudeInChrome.scenarios.description: Repo-relative path to the data file(s) describing what a Claude-in-Chrome session should check — case IDs, starting routes, expected outcomes. Data only, never selectors or code (e2e-engine-contract.md §1). Required only if 'claude-in-chrome' is listed in e2e.engines.

e2e.claudeInChrome.baseUrlEnv.description: Name of an environment variable — never a literal URL — that the qa-browser-explore skill reads for the target environment's base URL. Required only if 'claude-in-chrome' is listed in e2e.engines.

evidence.root.description: Repo-relative directory results and case evidence are written under, per e2e-engine-contract.md §4.

tracker.type.description: e.g. 'jira', 'linear', 'github-issues', or 'none'. Names which adapter the orchestrator skill should use to fetch/comment on a ticket — this kit does not implement the adapter itself.

tracker.projectKey.description: e.g. a Jira project key. Meaningless, and omittable, when tracker.type is 'none'.

publisher.type.description: e.g. 'confluence', 'notion', or 'none'. Where a rendered report gets published, if anywhere.

publisher.target.description: e.g. a Confluence space key. Omittable when publisher.type is 'none'.

router.enabled.description: Optional. 'true' to opt into tools/route-task.py's task/model tier recommendations; omit or 'false' to leave routing off (default). Advisory only — this kit never calls a model or switches one; see core/model-router-contract.md.

router.riskPaths.description: Optional, comma-separated glob patterns (fnmatch-style, repo-relative) that always force the 'deep' tier regardless of any other signal, e.g. 'src/services/auth*,src/**/*cognito*'. Meaningful only when router.enabled is 'true'; leaving it empty means no path-based risk escalation, not an error.

router.riskKeywords.description: Optional, comma-separated case-insensitive keywords matched against touched file paths and a task's free-text note, e.g. 'cognito,oauth,phi,payment'. Same always-'deep' effect as router.riskPaths.

router.tiers.fast.agent.description: Name of the subagent (or human process) route-task.py recommends for the 'fast' tier. Required only if router.enabled is 'true'.

router.tiers.standard.agent.description: Same, for the 'standard' tier. Required only if router.enabled is 'true'.

router.tiers.deep.agent.description: Same, for the 'deep' tier. Required only if router.enabled is 'true'.
